subject: general
question: ______ is the line of zero deviation and represents the basic size.
solution:
**Concept**

 
• **Basic Size:** This is the size of a part to which the limits of deviation are assigned. It is the theoretical size used for design calculations.
 
• **Zero Line:** In the graphical representation of limits and fits, the zero line is a straight line that corresponds to the basic size.
 
• **Deviation:** It is the algebraic difference between a size and the corresponding basic size. If the size is equal to the basic size, the deviation is zero.

**Explanation**

In metrology and engineering drawings, the **Zero Line** is used as a reference in the graphical representation of tolerances:

 
• The zero line represents the **basic size**.
 
• It is called the line of zero deviation because any point on this line has a deviation value of zero (since Size = Basic Size).
 
• Positive deviations (where the size is larger than the basic size) are shown above the zero line.
 
• Negative deviations (where the size is smaller than the basic size) are shown below the zero line.

By convention, the zero line is drawn as a horizontal line. The position of the tolerance zone is defined relative to this zero line.

**Conclusion**

**Hence, the Zero line is the line of zero deviation and represents the basic size.**</p
